title: At the window (Confessions 9.10)
hookLine: Augustine and Monica, rising in thought beyond all things
carry: we touched it for a moment
tomorrow: where do you keep the smell of lilies in a dark room?

cards: Some of the best talks happen side by side: in a car at night, on a porch, at the kitchen sink, nobody looking at anybody. Ostia, on the Tiber.

Augustine and his mother, Monica, are resting from a long journey before a sea voyage. One day the two of them are leaning at a window over the garden of the house where they're staying. No crowd, no noise.
A mother and her son, talking quietly. And the talk keeps climbing.

teach.b: They're talking about the life of the saints to come, the life Paul describes this way: "Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard."

teach.h: PAST THE SUN, MOON AND STARS.
teach.b: Step by step their thoughts rise, past everything bodily, past the earth, the sun, the moon and the stars, to their own minds, and beyond those too, toward the wisdom by which everything was made.

teach.h: ONE WHOLE BEAT OF THE HEART.
teach.b: And there, Augustine says, while they spoke of it and longed for it, they touched it, a little, with one whole beat of the heart. That's the answer to yesterday's question.

Then they sighed, and came back down to the sound of their own voices, where every word has a beginning and an end. Then Monica speaks. Son, she says, for my part nothing in this life delights me anymore.
There was one thing I wanted to stay for: to see you a Catholic Christian before I died. God has given me that, and more.

teach.h: WHAT AM I DOING HERE STILL?
teach.b: What am I doing here still?

teach.h: WE TOUCHED IT FOR A MOMENT.
teach.b: Not long after, Augustine tells us, she fell ill. Here's the detail to keep: this talk doesn't happen in a church. It happens at a window, between two people, and neither of them has all the words.

how: Christians remember Monica with a feast in some church calendars, and the window at Ostia is read as a picture of hope in the life to come, shared in conversation.

games.q: your aunt, just home from the hospital, starts talking at Sunday lunch about what comes after death. the table goes quiet. what fits the window at Ostia?
o: change the subject; it's too heavy for lunch.
lean in and talk with her, even without answers.

games.why: Augustine and Monica talked about the life to come, side by side. the talk itself was where they touched it.

practice: Pick up your phone and send one person a real question, not small talk: what do you hope heaven is like, or what's the most beautiful thing you've ever seen? Then set the phone face down and sit, whether or not they've answered.
